defects: The final 'filmstrip of posters' shot runs 5.9s and goes nearly static in the last second (change 1.1/s). That is dead air instead of a settled end.
Audio starts at about 1.9s. The first title card plays over near-silence and nothing hits under it.
Faint horizontal seam lines run across the opening SUB/STAT/ION frame at panel boundaries. They look like a compositing or tiling artifact.
The PAULA TEMPLE capacitor coil reads as flat vector clip-art: uniform orange ellipses with no believable shading. It also blocks letters, so 'PAULA' becomes hard to read.
The RROSE electric texture looks like a stock or procedural noise plate. It clashes with the warm, glowing rendering of the other shots.
In the KIA / IDA ENGBERG split frame, the second name is cut off at the bottom edge, and the panel joins have hard, unconsidered seams.
The 'DANGER' sign on PHASE FATALE is a literal signage gag. It breaks the dark, glowing palette with a large flat yellow field.
The glow halos are heavy and uniform on every word, so the type edges look soft and the bloom looks applied from a preset instead of lit.
gaps: Motion is mostly hard cuts between near-static posters, with no strips to show otherwise. The pairs show very little in-shot movement, nothing hands off from one element to the next, and the electrical metaphor (current and charge moving between artists) never drives the transitions. Top studios would route the energy physically from shot to shot.

Sound is a sparse click/impact grid plus one noise riser and a drop at about 11s. The spectrogram shows no tonal or harmonic layer, no bass design and no sounds specific to each device (hum, arc, relay clunk). It reads as generated or thin, not scored sound design.

Finish and system are inconsistent. Each shot has a different render language (vector coil, stock lightning, flat sign, bloom type), and the frame splits leave names cropped. Holding one lit material and keeping every frame poster-tight would lift this from competent to award level.
